US20060047201A1.title: Processing of continuous pressure-related signals derivable from a human or animal body or body cavity
US20060047201A1.abstract: A method for processing pressure signals derived from locations inside or outside a human or animal body cavity. Different aspects relate to differentiating between cardiac beat- and artifact-induced pressure waves, obtaining new information from pressure signals, and predicting pressures inside a body cavity. Devices and a system for sensing continuous pressure signals and displaying output. Other features relate to draining fluid from a brain or spinal fluid cavity.
US20060047201A1.key_disclosure: The patent explicitly states: 'in case of suspected shunt dysfunction, computation of said TS.x parameters provides new information whether suspected shunt malfunction includes over- or under-drainage.' This DIRECTLY teaches temporal pressure-signal processing for shunt malfunction diagnosis.
what_it_teaches: Continuous pressure signal processing from body cavities including intracranial
Temporal parameters (TS.x) computed from pressure time-series
Differentiating cardiac beat-induced pressure waves from artifacts
Assessing pressure signal quality (good vs bad)
Determining whether suspected shunt malfunction includes over- or under-drainage
Pressure monitoring related to CSF drainage from brain/spinal fluid cavity
Sensor drift compensation (addresses atmospheric pressure changes and sensor drift)

C2_limitations_addressed.CL5a_continuous_pressure_acquisition: ADDRESSED — teaches continuous pressure signal acquisition from body cavities
C2_limitations_addressed.CL5b_temporal_feature_extraction: ADDRESSED — teaches TS.x temporal parameters from pressure time-series
C2_limitations_addressed.CL5c_obstruction_vs_confounder_classific: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED — teaches distinguishing shunt malfunction (over/under-drainage) but does NOT specifically teach distinguishing obstruction from posture/cough/drift
C2_limitations_addressed.CL5d_drift_compensation: ADDRESSED — explicitly addresses sensor drift and atmospheric pressure changes
C2_limitations_addressed.CL5e_continuous_obstruction_decision: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED — provides information about shunt malfunction but does not describe a continuous automated obstruction decision algorithm

what_it_does_NOT_teach: Endovascular eShunt-specific anatomy (CL2, CL3) — patent is about traditional ICP monitoring
Differential CSF-venous pressure (CL4) — teaches absolute pressure, not differential

Specific classification of obstruction vs posture vs cough vs drift as distinct temporal signatures (CL5c) — teaches over/under-drainage distinction but not the specific confounder discrimination C2 proposes
eShunt-specific integration (CL3) — traditional ICP monitoring context

US9668663B2.title: Implantable dual sensor bio-pressure transponder and method of calibration
US9668663B2.abstract: A bio-pressure sensor system comprising a first sensor for reference pressure measurement and a second sensor for fluid pressure within a human body, with shared reference element and independent output signals.
US9668663B2.key_disclosure: Dual implantable pressure sensors with reference calibration, designed for CSF pressure measurement. Teaches: (1) dual-sensor architecture with reference element, (2) calibration method using known reference pressures, (3) drift compensation, (4) CSF pressure applications, (5) shunt context (7 mentions).

C2_limitations_addressed.CL4_differential_pressure: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED — dual sensor with reference measurement is architecturally similar to differential measurement, but patent focuses on calibration rather than CSF-venous differential
C2_limitations_addressed.CL5d_drift_compensation: ADDRESSED — 7 mentions of drift, 22 of calibration. Teaches drift compensation via reference sensor.

what_it_does_NOT_teach: Temporal signature classification for obstruction detection (CL5c)
Specific CSF-venous differential pressure (CL4 — uses reference sensor, not venous pressure)

2025_Neurology_waveform_study.title: Non-Invasive Intracranial Pressure Waveform Monitoring of Asymptomatic Patients with CSF Shunts Versus Patients with Shunt Dysfunction (P2-2.007)
2025_Neurology_waveform_study.finding: ICP waveform analysis (P2/P1 ratio, time-to-peak) is actively used to distinguish shunted patients with dysfunction from asymptomatic shunted patients
2025_Neurology_waveform_study.impact_on_C2: Demonstrates that temporal waveform analysis for shunt dysfunction is not merely theoretical — it is being used clinically. This makes it harder to argue that applying temporal analysis to shunt pressure is non-obvious.
what_it_does_NOT_teach: Specific drift-compensation in an implanted endovascular sensor

expanded_section_103_attack.motivation_to_combine: STRONG — a POSITA working on CSF shunt monitoring would be motivated to combine: (1) shunt pressure sensing (US8870787), (2) differential pressure (US10413710), (3) vascular placement (US10806352), (4) temporal signal processing for malfunction diagnosis (US20060047201A1), (5) drift compensation (US9668663B2), and (6) eShunt anatomy. All are in the same or adjacent fields.

H_C2_8.name: TEMPORAL_PROCESSING_ALREADY_KNOWN
H_C2_8.description: Continuous pressure signals, waveform features and temporal analysis were already used to diagnose or characterize shunt dysfunction before C2 (US20060047201A1 + 2025 clinical evidence).
H_C2_8.evidence: US20060047201A1 explicitly teaches TS.x temporal parameters for shunt malfunction diagnosis. 2025 Neurology study shows clinical use of waveform analysis for shunt dysfunction.
H_C2_8.implication: C2 cannot claim 'temporal pressure analysis for shunt obstruction' as novel. Must narrow to specific technical contribution.

H_C2_9.name: ONLY_SPECIFIC_COMBINATION_NOVEL
H_C2_9.description: Individual components are known, but the claimed combination of eShunt-specific differential CSF/venous pressure + temporal confounder discrimination + continuous obstruction inference is non-obvious.
H_C2_9.evidence_for: No reference teaches CSF-venous DIFFERENTIAL pressure waveform for obstruction classification (CL5d). No reference teaches continuous automated eShunt-integrated obstruction decision (CL5e).
H_C2_9.evidence_against: The combination motivation is strong (all in same field). The 2025 clinical evidence shows the field is actively developing waveform analysis for shunt dysfunction. The gap between 'ICP waveform analysis' and 'CSF-venous differential waveform analysis' may be narrow.
H_C2_9.implication: C2's defensible novelty is now VERY NARROW: specifically CL5d (differential CSF-venous waveform features) and CL5e (continuous eShunt-integrated decision). If these are found to be obvious modifications, C2 may not survive.

updated_C2_assessment.new: HIGH PRIOR-ART THREAT — CL5 broad form is prior-art-threatened by US20060047201A1. Novel remainder narrows to CL5d (CSF-venous differential waveform) and CL5e (continuous eShunt-integrated decision). The combination motivation is strong. C2's survival depends on whether these two elements are non-obvious.
updated_C2_assessment.defensible_novelty: VERY NARROW: (1) CSF-venous DIFFERENTIAL pressure waveform features for obstruction classification (not absolute ICP waveform), (2) continuous automated obstruction decision integrated into eShunt anatomy. Everything else is taught by the 6-reference combination.
updated_C2_assessment.what_would_kill_C2: Finding prior art teaching differential CSF-venous pressure waveform analysis (not just absolute ICP) for shunt obstruction. OR: finding that a POSITA would naturally apply differential measurement to the waveform analysis taught by US20060047201A1.
updated_C2_assessment.what_would_save_C2: Proving that CSF-venous DIFFERENTIAL waveform features provide materially better obstruction discrimination than absolute ICP waveform features alone (scientific test). AND: confirming no prior art teaches this specific differential waveform approach.

scientific_attack_required.experiment: Compare obstruction classification performance: absolute ICP waveform vs CSF-venous DIFFERENTIAL waveform
scientific_attack_required.hypothesis: If differential waveform provides materially better discrimination (sensitivity/specificity) than absolute ICP waveform, CL5d is strengthened. If not, CL5d collapses and C2 likely dies.
scientific_attack_required.method: Simulate both signals under obstruction, posture, cough, drift conditions. Compare classification accuracy. This is the SCIENTIFIC test that determines whether C2's narrowest defensible novelty (CL5d) is technically meaningful.
scientific_attack_required.connection_to_patent: This is the patent-physics loop: prior-art search narrows novelty to CL5d → scientific test determines if CL5d provides technical advantage → result updates patent assessment.
